title: What TinyAgent is
text: TinyAgent is a minimal, modular, educational agent framework. An LLM only turns text into text; the harness, the code around the model, is what makes it an agent. TinyAgent is that harness, small enough to read in a minute.

title: The agent loop
text: The agent loop is: task, memory, the LLM decides, an action, a tool, an observation, and then back to the start until the task is done. The public entry point is run(task). The private method _step(task) builds the prompt, asks the LLM and returns an answer or an action. The private method _execute_action(action) dispatches to a tool and returns an observation.

title: Components
text: TinyAgent has four components. llm is the brain that reasons and picks the next step. memory is the context holding past messages and observations. tools are the hands: functions that act on the world. planner is the strategy that splits a goal into sub-steps. All four are placeholders today and are added step by step.

title: Roadmap
text: The roadmap is built step by step. Done: the agent skeleton with control-flow stubs, and the Sphinx documentation. Next: Step 1 LLM integration, Step 2 Memory, Step 3 Tools, Step 4 Planning.

title: Models used
text: The project studies two local models served by Ollama. gemma3:4b is the baseline: it has no native reasoning and no native tool calling. gemma4:e4b-it-qat is the agentic model, trained for reasoning and tool calling. Both are 4B-class, so differences come from training, not size.

title: Running the project
text: Create a virtual environment and run python main.py, which prints 'Received: Hello, agent!'. Build the documentation with python -m sphinx -b html -n -W --keep-going docs docs/_build/html and open docs/_build/html/index.html. Pull the models with ollama pull gemma3:4b and ollama pull gemma4:e4b-it-qat.

title: Hardware notes
text: The development machine has an RTX 3060 Laptop GPU with 6 GB of VRAM and about 16 GB of RAM. gemma3:4b fits entirely in VRAM. gemma4:e4b-it-qat is about 6.1 GB, so a small part runs on the CPU. Use ollama ps to see the GPU and CPU split of a loaded model.
